newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-KALLIS GETS ONE OF THREE MIDDLESEX TONS.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-KALLIS GETS ONE OF THREE MIDDLESEX TONS.

text.p: South African Jacques Kallis and Middlesex perennials Mark Ramprakash and Mike Gatting all scored centuries to give their side a firm grip on their County championship match against Northamptonshire at Lord's on Thursday.

They ended the first day on 400 for two as Ramprakash, captaining the side for the first time since Gatting relinquished the post this week, made the perfect start by winning the toss and electing to bat.
Kallis and Paul Weekes then made kept the initiative by forging Middlesex's first century opening partnership of the season.

Weekes drove Kevin Curran to Jeremy Snape in the covers after making 41 and with the total on 107, but that only made it worse for Northants as Ramprakash then joined Kallis, who was awarded his county cap during the tea interval.

The South African, who has been in prime form, duly completed his first century for the county midway through the afternoon before being out to the same combination that got Weekes after making 121 including 21 boundaries and an all-run four from just 162 deliveries.
Gatting then joined his successor as captain and they stayed together until the close to adding an unbroken 181 for the third wicket.
Both completed centuries during the last half hour of play, with Ramprakash's 109 his third first class hundred of the season and his second in the championship.
Gatting's 102 not out was his 92nd career first class century and, without the responsibilities of captaincy, he could complete a century of hundreds before the season's end.
On a gloriously sunny day for bastmen, Andy Moles was in fine form for Warwickshire against Hampshire at Southampton.
Moles made a magnificent 168 in six hours at the crease and featured in stands of 154 and 184 respectively with Nick Knight (81) and David Hemp (76 not out) as Warwickshire closed at 351 for two.
Teenager Derek Kenway, making his debut, claimed Moles's scalp by having him caught at square leg by Matthew Hayden.
Openers Steve James and Hugh Morris shared a double century stand to put Glamorgan in the driving seat with a massive 433 for three against Durham at Cardiff.
The partnership was finally broken on 229 by off-spinner James Boiling, who caught and bowled James for 153. Morris was finally out for 135.
Yorkshire paceman Darren Gough had another good day following his fine efforts for England in the one-day series against Australia last week.
He landed another five-wicket haul, this time for 74, as the visitors kept Essex down to 297 all out at Ilford. Yorkshire were 158 for five in reply with Michael Vaughan making 92 not out.
Matthew Fleming grabbed five Nottinghamshire wickets for 51 from 28.5 overs bats as Kent bowled the home side out for 216 at Trent Bridge.
Usman Afzaal, 19, from Pakistan, top scored on 54 and Graeme Archer made 49 as Notts claimed only one batting point with Kent taking four bowling points. In reply, Kent were 39 for one at the close.
